name: Canola
summary: Canola is hardly grown in the Philippines. The canola oil sold here comes from abroad. It wants cool weather, so the few who try it are highland growers in places like Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon, who sow it in the cool dry months the way they sow its cousins mustasa and pechay. This short guide shows that way.
season: Only in the highlands, sown at the end of the rains, around October to December, so it grows and flowers in the cool dry months and ripens before the hot months. The lowlands are too hot for it to set good seed.
material: Small round seed of a spring type canola. Winter types sold in cold countries need a long cold spell before they flower and will not flower well here. The seed is sown dry and shallow, like mustard seed.
spacing: Sown in rows on raised beds and thinned so the plants stand a little apart. Growers here have no settled spacing yet.
water: Light sprinkling after sowing and in dry spells, as for highland vegetables. Too much water at the end delays ripening.
fertilizer: Manure or compost in the beds before sowing, then ammonium sulfate (21 0 0) as a side dress for nitrogen and sulfur. Canola also needs enough boron.
care: Thinning, hand weeding, light watering, and checking for the same pests that attack cabbage and mustard. Bees visiting the flowers help it set more seed.
harvest: Ready when most pods are brown and the seeds black and hard. Plants are cut in the morning before the pods split, dried on mats, threshed by beating, winnowed and dried again.

ways.label: Sown in rows on beds

steps.title: Make fine beds
steps.how: Dig or plow the plot, break the clods and make raised beds as for highland vegetables. Mix in well rotted manure or compost.

steps.title: Sow in shallow rows
steps.how: Draw shallow lines across the bed, scatter the seed thinly along them and cover with a little fine soil. Water gently with a sprinkler.

steps.title: Thin and weed
steps.how: Pull out crowded seedlings so the plants stand a little apart, and pull the weeds while they are small.

steps.title: Side dress
steps.how: Put ammonium sulfate (21 0 0) beside the rows and water it in. Canola needs a lot of sulfur, which this fertilizer also gives.

steps.title: Watch for cabbage pests
steps.how: Check the leaves for the same worms, aphids and flea beetles that attack cabbage and mustard, and pick off what you can early.

steps.title: Cut before the pods split
steps.how: When most pods have turned from green to brown and the seeds inside are black and hard, cut the plants in the morning before the pods split open.

steps.title: Dry and thresh
steps.how: Dry the cut plants on a mat or tarp, beat them to free the seeds, winnow and dry the seed well before storing it.

ways.note: Days from sowing, taken as about 100 days. The pods ripen over about six to eight weeks after flowering starts, and timing in our highlands still varies.

mistakes: Trying it in the hot lowlands, where it sets little seed.
Buying a winter type that needs cold to flower.
Leaving the pods until they split and drop the seed.
Giving no sulfur or boron, which leaves pods half empty.
better: Try a small plot first in the cool months before planting more.
Use a spring type seed and have the soil tested.
Use ammonium sulfate or another sulfur source for nitrogen.
Keep bees nearby and harvest on time, before the pods split.
